biography: Jörg Müller, a name synonymous with flamboyant racing and unwavering determination, hails from Düsseldorf, Germany. From a young age, Jörg was captivated by the roar of engines, spending countless hours tinkering with go-karts in his father's garage. His entry into professional racing was meteoric, quickly ascending through the ranks of Formula Ford before making a splash in the Porsche Supercup. His defining moment came at the 24 Hours of Nürburgring, where, despite starting near the back of the grid due to a qualifying mishap, he relentlessly carved his way through the field, ultimately securing a podium finish in a privately entered Porsche. Now, as a veteran driver, Jörg continues to compete, balancing his passion for racing with mentoring young drivers and running his own racing academy.
drivingStyle: Jörg Müller's driving style is best described as aggressive and opportunistic. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to take risks, often pushing his car to the absolute limit. He possesses an uncanny ability to extract maximum performance from his tires, even in the most challenging conditions. While some may criticize his aggressive approach, there's no denying his raw speed and his knack for finding every last ounce of performance.

careerHighlight: Winning the Spa 24 Hours in 2003 with the BMW M3 E46 GTR. He drove the final stint, holding off intense pressure from the pursuing Ferrari to secure a memorable victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2008. A mechanical failure caused a high-speed accident, sidelining his team and costing him a potential victory.
